### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, a group of three mutually exclusive activities sat between A41 and A26: A19 occurred in about 35 in 100 traces, A25 in about 35 in 100 and A20 in about 30 in 100, and the three essentially never appeared in the same trace. [REL007, REL009, REL014, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- Before, A41 was followed by A19 in about 33% of its observed outgoing transitions, by A25 in about 33% and by A20 in about 27%, and each of the three led almost always on to A26 (about 97–99% of their outgoing transitions). [DIR004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR002]
- In the later window, A19 and A25 are not observed in any of the 200 traces, and A20 appears in only 1 of 200. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC002]
- In the later window, A41 is followed directly by A26 in about 92 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; before, no direct A41–A26 transition was observed. Accordingly, A26 follows A41 within one event position in about 93 in 100 traces, whereas before this never happened and the pair was almost always two positions apart (about 93 in 100). [DIR004, LAG002]
- Pairwise relations mirror this: before, A19, A20 and A25 each followed A14 (about 30–35 in 100 traces, always after A14) and A41 (about 30–35 in 100, always after A41), and preceded A26 and A31; in the later window these pairs almost always appear as one activity occurring without the other, since only A14, A41, A26 and A31 of these still occur. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL012, REL017, REL021, REL010, REL011, REL015, REL016, REL019, REL020]
- A26 now occurs slightly earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.39 before vs 0.37 after) and A41 slightly later (about 0.32 vs 0.33), with both present in all traces in both windows; the positional gap between them roughly halved. [POS005, POS006]
- The distance from A24 to A31 tightened: before, A31 followed A24 most often two positions later (about 59 in 100 cases), after, most often one position later (about 59 in 100). [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, A41 leads directly to A26, whereas in the earlier window A41 led to one of three alternatives — A19, A25 or A20, each used in roughly a third of traces and essentially never together — which in turn led almost invariably to A26. In the later window this intermediate block is no longer routed through: A19 and A25 are unobserved, A20 appears in a single trace, and A41's transitions go straight to A26. [DIR004, LAG002, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]

The hypothesis rests on direct relational evidence, not on participation alone: the successor profile of A41 changed from A19/A25/A20 to A26 with about 200 outgoing-transition observations in each window, and the A41–A26 pair distance collapsed from two event positions (about 93 in 100 traces) to one (about 93 in 100). The shift is consistent across about 36 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.61 expected by chance in that family — far beyond what random re-splits produce — including the relations of the three activities with A14, A31 and A26, and the positional shifts of A41 and A26 point the same way. [DIR004, LAG002, REL012, REL017, REL021, REL010, REL015, REL019, POS005, POS006]

Limitations: zero participation only establishes that A19, A20 and A25 were not observed in the later window, so the evidence cannot distinguish removing these activities from keeping them while always routing around them; and the single later trace containing A20, in which A20 was followed by A30 and sat later in the trace, rests on one observation and cannot be interpreted. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, POS003]

Other differences: the A24–A31 distance tightened from mostly two positions to mostly one, and A14, which all traces contain, shows only a negligible positional shift. [LAG001, POS001]
